summary: A neck collar cut from one flat sheet. It packs flat, twists open, and locks with three tabs — no glue, no screws. Nobody has folded one yet: the page behind this card is a drawing, and it says so.
license_note: MIT is what this card's #vc-card block declares, on disk and in the deployed page, and it is the host repo's own grant — GitHub's licence API returns spdx_id MIT for mrdirno/vibe-cards, read anonymously 2026-08-17 with x-ratelimit-limit 60 proving the call carried no token. NOTICE at the repo root is the file that removes material from that grant; it is served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt (200, measured the same day). Measured, because a silent exclusion and no exclusion read alike: `grep -icE 'kaze' NOTICE` returns 1, and that single hit is inside a quoted grep command in the Compound Craft section, not a withheld path — so no card 007 file is withheld today. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds, and nothing here withholds anything NOTICE does not: if a later pass finds this artwork is not the project's to grant, NOTICE is the file that says so, and this sentence does not survive it. Replication terms, as the card's own #vc-card block states them: replication "open" — the faces and the cutting file may be reproduced, including sold, with the copyright line travelling with them. Two MIT copyright lines cover the same material and neither is this file's to reconcile: the repo root LICENSE reads "Copyright (c) 2026 Aldrin Payopay / Persona 500 LLC", and the package's own examples/kaze-card/docs/LICENSE reads "Copyright (c) 2026 Kaze-Kiri Craft" — a name that appears in exactly one file in this repo, that one. That package licence is the full canonical MIT text (1072 bytes; the grant, sublicense and warranty clauses each grep once), unlike card 006's, which arrived by the same route as a 63-byte stub with no grant clause at all and was replaced with the canonical text in commit 47ba30c (63 bytes at 47ba30c^, 1088 now). It sits in docs/ rather than at the package root, so `ls examples/*/LICENSE` does not find it.
origin: Not a fork: GitHub reports fork=false and private=false for mrdirno/vibe-cards (read anonymously 2026-08-17, x-ratelimit-limit 60). /kaze/ is a page-project inside that repo, published on its Pages surface, and its MIT is INHERITED from the host repo's LICENSE rather than chosen for it. THE PACKAGE WAS NOT MADE HERE, and criterion 5 is the reason to say so plainly. examples/kaze-card/ arrived finished from another system: docs/FREEZE_MANIFEST.json names its three inputs — ONE_ENGINE_FRAMEWORK.md "probe-and-execute v2.1.1", TARGET_WISH_IT_BETTER_CARD.md and CARD_BRIEF_NEXT.md — and `git ls-files` matches none of the three anywhere in this repo. docs/AUTHORSHIP.md declares the stripe generator, the Kresling-Miura solver, the 1:1 SVG and all README text as AI-generated, with the human contribution named as selections and arrangement. The commit that took it in is 429365a, 2026-08-16, authored by `Agent-1 <agent@resonance.ai>`, titled "Card 007 into Card Studio: the pair, the faces, and the intake record"; it names three defects fixed before anything printed — a calibration ruler labelled 0 to 20 mm that spanned 79.5 mm of card, two proofing guides drawn inside the face, and a QR that "pointed nowhere until intake burned in the real address". That last one is checkable now: the package shipped its QR payload as the literal string CARD_URL_PENDING (docs/FREEZE_MANIFEST.json seeds.qr_payload and README ASSUMPTIONS), while `./tools/qrdecode src/site/kaze/card-back.png` returns https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/kaze/ today and the same command on card-front.png returns NO BARCODE DETECTED — so the address was burned in here, and this card carries exactly one code, on its back. The artwork is procedural rather than photographic and depicts no person: docs/EULOGY.md kill 1 records a workshop-pair front killed for "casting complexity and likeness risk" before generation. Inside its own book this card is a compounding step, not a spinoff: it consumes tools from cards 001 through 006, and the package's own docs/wish-it-better.json declares origin "ZARIA-HALO-006" — borrowed geometry between two cards in one repo, which is lineage, not a fork of a separate project. ONE CLAIM THIS PACKAGE MAKES DOES NOT RESOLVE, and it is disclosed here because a sibling manifest in the same batch already records it against this card: examples/kaze-card/package/index.html:343 and docs/README.md:40 both list a "tab-and-slot solver from MANIS-CUIRASS-001" among the capabilities this card consumes, and no such solver exists — `grep -ril solver examples/manis-card` returns nothing, and MANIS's own manifest says the same of itself. The tab geometry lives in that card's blueprint raster and in the numbers printed on its face, not in code. The consumed-capability list is therefore an intent recorded by the arriving package, not an inventory of things a reader can call.
_note: WHY L0 AND NOT L1. L0's three clauses hold and nothing more is claimed. (1) The spec file is present: WISH_IT_BETTER.md is tracked at the host repo root, 200 at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md and 200 at raw.githubusercontent on main, against a 404 control on the same host in the same run. (2) A LICENSE with a real SPDX id: MIT, from the licence API, anonymously. (3) A wish channel that works: this page's own well, measured below. NOT L1, on both of its clauses. L1 needs wishes to reach a terminal state, and there is no evidence any wish for this card has reached one — the well went live 2026-08-16 and the queue cannot be read from outside: an anonymous select with the page's own key returns HTTP 200 and `[]`, which is row-level security filtering and is indistinguishable from an empty table, so it proves no disclosure and nothing about terminal states. L1 also needs every shipped change to carry an eval meeting §2; the seven entries in this page's log are real corrections with numbers, but they were found by this repo's own passes rather than moved through a wish queue, and I did not audit the seven commits touching this card against §2 one by one. The spec settles the tie in the same direction twice: §7 says start at L0 because it is honest, and §5 says even the v1.0.1 amendment earns nobody L2. WISH CHANNEL — the page, not a mailto, and not the landing page's well. The deployed /kaze/ page carries exactly one `data-wish-well` marker, on the button that opens its own well (measured 2026-08-17 in the served bytes, last-modified Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:32:21 GMT), and that button posts to a Supabase REST table with a public anon-role key embedded in the page — no account, no mail client, no address, which §4 says beats a mailto because it is a queue with a status a loop can move. The endpoint answers: an anonymous GET returns 200. I did NOT post a wish, so THE INSERT PATH IS UNVERIFIED BY ME — the registry's own curation note records a previous audit putting probe rows into the maintainer's live production queue and concludes the next one should read the deployed bytes rather than post. The package's own docs/wish-it-better.json declares `mailto:wish@compound-crafts.example`, which cannot reach anyone: .example is reserved by RFC 2606 and `dig NS example.` returns nothing here. This file replaces that route rather than repeating it. I declare the bare page url and not `.../kaze/#wish`: the builder's derived manifests use that anchor and the landing page really has `id="wish"`, but the deployed /kaze/ page does not, so on this page the fragment points at nothing. Both forms pass the gate, which strips the fragment before fetching; the bare url is the one that is true. WHAT THIS FILE CLOSES. Measured 2026-08-17, one run, same host: https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/kaze/wish-it-better.json 404, a freshly-invented control path 404, /wish-it-better.json 200. tools/build_site.py can DERIVE this file, but only for entries already in network.json listed[] — so a derived manifest would be produced BY the act of listing, which makes criterion 4 self-satisfying. This one is hand-authored and committed before listing, the shape src/site/gt/wish-it-better.json set. The asset rglob over src/site/ ships it either way, so it publishes at the card's own url whether or not this card is ever listed; if it is listed, build_site.py keeps this file rather than deriving over it, and fails the build if this `level` and the registry badge disagree. NOT GATED TODAY, said rather than left to be discovered: nothing reads this file's wish_channel. Check 7 in tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs reads only the artifact-root manifest, and the --network-registry mode that fetches per-entry manifests iterates listed entries only, and KAZE-KIRI-007 is not in listed[]. Every claim here stands on the measurement quoted beside it, not on a gate. WHAT A CARD HOLDER NEEDS THAT THE FIELDS ABOVE CANNOT CARRY. Nobody has cut or folded this collar. As drawn, the lock does not fit — measured on examples/kaze-card/assets/KAZE-KIRI-007_1to1.svg, the tab leaves the sheet 10 mm tall (`M 439.823 10 ... L 439.823 20`) and the notch it enters is an 8 mm opening (`M 0 11 L 10 11 L 10 19 L 0 19`). The package's spec table cited a 0.46 mm slot and 0.15 mm clearance; in that file `0.46` occurs zero times and `0.15` occurs once, inside a caption <text> element, so neither is a feature of the drawing. The full-size cutting file is not on the page at all, and the card sends a reader there for it. The chip's address can never change, so those are things the page has to absorb; a reprint cannot fix a card already in a hand.
